readings.title: The Man from Uts
readings.subtitle: Blameless and Upright
readings.text: [Job 1:1] There was a man in the land of Uts, whose name was Iyoḇ. And that man was perfect and straight, and one who feared <dn>Elohim</dn> and turned aside from evil. [2] And seven sons and three daughters were born to him. [3] And his possessions were seven thousand sheep, and three thousand camels, and five hundred yoke of oxen, and five hundred female donkeys, and a very great body of servants, so that this man was the greatest of all the people of the East. [4] And his sons went and held a feast in the house of each on his day, and sent and invited their three sisters to eat and to drink with them. [5] And it came to be, when the days of feasting had gone round, that Iyoḇ would send and set them apart, and he would rise early in the morning and offer ascending offerings – the number of them all – for Iyoḇ said, “It might be that my sons have sinned and cursed <dn>Elohim</dn> in their hearts.” This Iyoḇ did always.

readings.title: The First Trial
readings.subtitle: The Sifting of Possessions
readings.text: [Job 1:6] And the day came to be that the sons of <dn>Elohim</dn> came to present themselves before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and Satan also came among them. [7] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Satan, <dq>“From where do you come?”</dq> And Satan answered <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and said, “From diligently searching in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.” [8] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Satan, <dq>“Have you set your heart on <dn>My</dn> servant Iyoḇ, that there is none like him on the earth, a perfect and straight man, one who fears <dn>Elohim</dn> and turns aside from evil?”</dq> [9] And Satan answered <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and said, “Is Iyoḇ fearing <dn>Elohim</dn> for naught? [10] “Have <dn>You</dn> not made a hedge around him, and around his household, and around all that he has on every side? <dn>You</dn> have blessed the work of his hands, and his livestock have increased in the land. [11] “But stretch out <dn>Your</dn> hand, please, and strike all that he has – if he would not curse <dn>You</dn> to <dn>Your</dn> face!” [12] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Satan, <dq>“See, all that he has is in your hand. Only do not lay a hand on himself.”</dq> And Satan went out from the presence of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [13] And the day came to be when his sons and his daughters were eating and drinking wine in their oldest brother’s house, [14] and a messenger came to Iyoḇ and said, “The oxen were ploughing and the donkeys feeding alongside them, [15] when Sheḇa fell upon them and took them away, and they smote <dn>את</dn> the servants with the edge of the sword, and I alone have escaped to report to you!” [16] While this one was speaking, another came and said, “The fire of <dn>Elohim</dn> fell from the heavens and burned up the sheep and the servants, and consumed them, and I alone have escaped to report to you!” [17] While this one was speaking, another came and said, “The Kasdim made out three bands, and raided the camels and took them away, and they smote <dn>את</dn> the servants with the edge of the sword, and I alone have escaped to report to you!” [18] While this one was speaking, another came and said, “Your sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in their oldest brother’s house, [19] and see, a great wind came from the wilderness and struck the four corners of the house, and it fell on the young men, and they are dead, and I alone have escaped to report to you!” [20] Then Iyoḇ rose up and tore <dn>את</dn> his robe, and shaved <dn>את</dn> his head, and fell to the ground and bowed himself, [21] and said, “Naked I came from my mother’s womb, and naked I return there. <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has given, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has taken away. Blessed be the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.” [22] In all this Iyoḇ did not sin nor ascribe folly to <dn>Elohim</dn>.

readings.title: The Second Trial
readings.subtitle: Bone and Flesh
readings.text: [Job 2:1] And the day came to be that the sons of <dn>Elohim</dn> came to present themselves before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and Satan also came among them to present himself before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [2] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Satan, <dq>“From where do you come?”</dq> And Satan answered <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and said, “From diligently searching in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.” [3] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Satan, <dq>“Have you set your heart on <dn>My</dn> servant Iyoḇ, that there is none like him on the earth, a perfect and straight man, one who fears <dn>Elohim</dn> and turns aside from evil? And still he holds fast to his integrity, although you incited <dn>Me</dn> against him, to destroy him without cause.”</dq> [4] And Satan answered <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and said, “Skin for skin! And all that a man has he gives for his life. [5] “But stretch out <dn>Your</dn> hand, please, and strike his bone and his flesh – if he would not curse <dn>You</dn> to <dn>Your</dn> face!” [6] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Satan, <dq>“See, he is in your hand, only spare <dn>את</dn> his life.”</dq> [7] And Satan went out from the presence of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and struck <dn>את</dn> Iyoḇ with painful boils from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head. [8] And he took a potsherd with which to scrape himself while he sat in the midst of the ashes. [9] And his wife said to him, “Do you still hold fast to your integrity? Curse <dn>Elohim</dn> and die!” [10] But he said to her, “You speak as one of the foolish women speaks. Indeed, should we accept only <dn>את</dn> good from <dn>Elohim</dn>, and not accept <dn>את</dn> evil?” In all this Iyoḇ did not sin with his lips.

readings.title: The Silence of Friends
readings.subtitle: Seven Days of Mourning
readings.text: [Job 2:11] And three friends of Iyoḇ heard of <dn>את</dn> all this evil that had come upon him, and each one came from his own place: Eliphaz the Tĕmanite, and Bildad the Shuḥite, and Tsophar the Na‛amathite. And they met together to come to mourn with him, and to comfort him. [12] And they lifted up their eyes from a distance and did not recognize him. And they lifted up their voices and wept, and each one tore his robe and sprinkled dust on his head toward the heavens. [13] And they sat down with him on the ground seven days and seven nights, and no one spoke a word to him, for they saw that his pain was very great.

readings.title: Job's Lament
readings.subtitle: Cursing the Day of Birth
readings.text: [Job 3:1] After this Iyoḇ opened <dn>את</dn> his mouth and cursed <dn>את</dn> his day. [2] And Iyoḇ spoke and said, [3] “Let the day perish on which I was born, and the night that said, ‘A male is conceived.’ [4] “Let that day be darkness. Let not <dn>Eloah</dn> from above seek for it, nor let light shine upon it. [5] “Let darkness and the shadow of death claim it. Let a cloud dwell upon it. Let the blackness of the day terrify it. [6] “That night – let thick darkness seize it. Let it not rejoice among the days of the year, let it not come into the number of the months. [7] “Look, let that night be barren! Let no singing come into it! [8] “Let those curse it who curse the day, who are skilled to rouse Lewyathan. [9] “Let the stars of its twilight be dark. Let it look for light, but have none, and let it not see the eyelids of the morning. [10] “Because it did not shut the doors of my mother’s womb, nor hid sorrow from my eyes. [11] “Why did I not die at birth? Come forth from the womb and expire? [12] “Why were the knees to receive me? Or why the breasts that I should nurse? [13] “For now I would have lain still and been at rest. I would have slept then, I would have been at peace, [14] “With sovereigns and counsellors of the earth, who built ruins for themselves, [15] “Or with princes who had gold, who filled their houses with silver; [16] “Or why was I not hidden like a stillborn child, like infants who never saw light? [17] “There the wrong ones cease from raging, and there the weary are at rest. [18] “Together prisoners shall be at ease; they shall not hear the voice of the oppressor. [19] “The small and great are there, and the servant is free from his master. [20] “Why is light given to him who is in misery, and life to the bitter of soul, [21] “Who are waiting for death, but it does not come, and search for it more than for hidden treasures; [22] “Who rejoice exceedingly, and are glad when they find the grave? [23] “To a man whose way is hidden, and whom <dn>Eloah</dn> has hedged in? [24] “For my sighing comes before I eat, and my groanings pour out like water. [25] “For the fear I feared has come upon me, and what I dreaded has befallen me. [26] “I have not been at ease, nor have I been undisturbed, nor have I been at rest, yet trouble comes.”

readings.title: Eliphaz Speaks
readings.subtitle: The Innocent Do Not Perish
readings.text: [Job 4:1] And Eliphaz the Tĕmanite answered and said, [2] “If one attempts a word with you, would you be weary? But who is able to withhold himself from speaking? [3] “See, you have instructed many, and you have strengthened weak hands. [4] “Your words have upheld him who was stumbling, and you have strengthened the feeble knees. [5] “But now it comes upon you, and you are weary. It strikes you, and you are troubled. [6] “Is not your reverence your confidence? And the integrity of your ways your expectation? [7] “Remember, please, who ever perished being innocent? Or where were the straight ones cut off? [8] “As I have seen, those who plough wickedness and sow trouble reap the same. [9] “By the breath of <dn>Eloah</dn> they perish, and by the spirit of <dn>His</dn> nostrils they are consumed. [10] “The roaring of the lion, and the voice of the fierce lion, and the teeth of the young lions are broken. [11] “The old lion perishes for lack of prey, and the cubs of the lioness are scattered. [12] “And a word was brought to me stealthily, and my ear received a whisper of it. [13] “In thoughts from visions of the night, when deep sleep falls on men, [14] “Fear came upon me, and trembling, which made all my bones shake. [15] “Then a spirit passed before my face, the hair of my flesh stood up. [16] “It stood still, but I could not discern its appearance. A form was before my eyes; there was silence, then I heard a voice saying: [17] ‘Is mortal man more righteous than <dn>Eloah</dn>? Is a strong man purer than his <dn>Maker</dn>? [18] ‘See, <dn>He</dn> puts no trust in <dn>His</dn> servants, and <dn>He</dn> charges <dn>His</dn> messengers with folly. [19] ‘How much more those who dwell in houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust, crushed before a moth? [20] ‘From morning to evening they are beaten down. They perish forever, with no one regarding. [21] ‘Is not their tent-cord torn away? They die, and not in wisdom.’
